column2: Rethinking Latency Denial-of-Service: Attacking the LLM Serving Framework, Not the Model
column8: The attacker is a black-box tenant with only public API access and no knowledge of model parameters or runtime internals.
column9: Fill and Squeeze: a black-box tenant exhausts the shared global KV pool (head-of-line blocking) and forces repeated preemption in vLLM v0.11.2 on L40S; benign co-located users see TTFT rise e.g. 0.15 s to 11.05 s (Qwen3-8B), up to 75-742x vs benign; uses inter-token latency as a side channel for KV occupancy; per-entity KV quota below saturation blocks Fill.
column10: Targets the KV cache pool and preemption directly and measures other tenants. Does not attack the prefix cache, eviction of cached prefixes, KV compression, or offload tiers (LMCache); setup is FCFS, LIFO preemption, no per-tenant quota; SGLang only in appendix.
column11: Closest prior art for KV-occupancy exhaustion. Any new KV-exhaustion idea must beat or differ from F&S (e.g., prefix-cache or compression-aware variants, or fair/quota schedulers). Small-model Metal reproduction plausible.

column2: Preserving Admission Responsibility in Multi-Tenant Large Language Model Prefix Caches
column8: A group that materializes new Key-Value (KV) blocks can force another to lose reusable state.
column9: Cross-tenant prefix-cache pollution is a recognized threat: adversary is a legitimate client controlling its own token sequences and timing; one-touch, low-and-slow rotation, and replay pollution patterns; PrefixShield implemented in vLLM 0.10.2 APC on L4/A100 restores victim hit ratio (abstract: 4.92% to 84.87% at 4096-block scale).
column10: Targets prefix-cache eviction specifically and measures victim hit ratio, but reports P95 TTFT nearly flat, so victim latency/cost harm is not shown as large; defense paper, not an attack-optimization paper; no compression, no offload tier, no adaptive attacker against PrefixShield.
column11: Most direct overlap with the advisor's 'prefix-cache attack tied to eviction' interest. Gap left: adaptive attacker vs PrefixShield, measured TTFT/cost harm, multi-tier (CPU/LMCache) pollution, and SGLang radix-tree eviction.

column2: An Engorgio Prompt Makes Large Language Model Babble on
column8: a malicious user crafts Engorgio prompts to intentionally increase the computation cost and latency of the inference process
column9: White-box optimized prompts suppress EOS so outputs approach max length on many open models; a real-world experiment shows threat to a resource-limited LLM service.
column10: Output-length/compute inflation only; does not target prefix cache, eviction, or compression explicitly; abstract does not measure effect on other tenants.
column11: Baseline 'long output' attacker; KV growth is a side effect. F&S reports such model-level attacks are largely isolated by batching.

column2: OverThink: Slowdown Attacks on Reasoning LLMs
column8: An adversary conducts the attack by injecting decoy reasoning problems into available content
column9: Indirect injection of decoy problems inflates hidden reasoning tokens (reported up to tens of x) while answers stay correct; common defenses largely ineffective.
column10: Reasoning-token/compute inflation only; no KV cache, prefix cache, eviction, or compression targeting; no measurement of other tenants in a shared server.
column11: Shows reasoning models give cheap length amplification that a KV-exhaustion attacker could use as a primitive.

column2: Sponge Examples: Energy-Latency Attacks on Neural Networks
column8: increasing energy consumption by a factor of 10 to 200
column9: Founding work: crafted inputs drive models toward worst-case energy and latency, language models especially vulnerable; portable across CPUs, GPUs, ASIC sim.
column10: Pre-LLM-serving; no KV cache, paging, prefix cache, or batching; no multi-tenant measurement.
column11: Origin citation for availability attacks; outside 2023-2026 window but defines the class.

column2: Fairness in Serving Large Language Models
column4: arXiv (cs.AI, cs.LG, cs.PF); venue not shown on page
column8: We prove a 2x tight upper bound on the service difference between two backlogged clients.
column9: VTC: token-level fair scheduler over continuous batching with a per-client counter; bounds service difference between backlogged clients.
column10: Fairness of compute/token service, not of KV memory or prefix-cache occupancy; abstract does not consider adversarial clients; no eviction or compression.
column11: The fairness baseline. Open question: does VTC bound harm when the attacker consumes KV memory or evicts cached prefixes rather than tokens of service?

column2: Adversarial Prompts for Acceptance Collapse in Speculative Decoding
column8: On the GSM8K dataset, our attack increases the mean sample time by 62.3% while preserving the task quality.
column9: ADSD adversarial suffixes collapse draft-target acceptance in speculative decoding, wasting compute while output quality holds.
column10: Targets speculative decoding acceptance, not KV cache, prefix cache, eviction, or compression; per search summary the threat model excludes KV-cache and scheduler manipulation; no other-tenant measurement.
column11: Adjacent availability vector; shows optimizations with data-dependent speedups can be inverted. Same logic applies to KV compression ratios.

column2: Mistletoe: Stealthy Acceleration-Collapse Attacks on Speculative Decoding
column8: a stealthy acceleration-collapse attack against speculative decoding
column9: Jointly optimizes lower drafter-target agreement and semantic preservation; reduces accepted length, collapses speedup and throughput, preserves quality.
column10: Speculative decoding only; no KV cache, prefix cache, eviction, or compression; no multi-tenant effect measured.
column11: Second independent 2026 paper; spec-decoding acceptance attacks are covered, not a gap.

column2: RepetitionCurse: Measuring and Understanding Router Imbalance in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs under DoS Stress
column8: out-of-distribution prompts can manipulate the routing strategy
column9: OOD repetitive prompts concentrate MoE expert routing, causing device imbalance, TTFT SLA violations, 3.063x end-to-end latency on Mixtral-8x7B.
column10: MoE expert routing, not KV cache, prefix cache, eviction, or compression; not request-level load balancers; other-tenant effect implied via SLA, not per-tenant measured in abstract.
column11: Template for 'efficiency optimization becomes DoS vector' framing; analogous framing fits KV compression.

column2: ThinkTrap: Denial-of-Service Attacks against Black-box LLM Services via Infinite Thinking
column8: as low as 1% of its original capacity
column9: Black-box derivative-free prompt optimization induces unbounded reasoning; at about 10 RPM the attack degrades service throughput to as low as 1% and sometimes causes complete failure.
column10: Output/reasoning length attack; does not target KV cache structure, prefix cache, eviction, or compression explicitly; service-wide throughput loss implies other users harmed but no per-tenant KV analysis.
column11: Shows rate limits in requests do not stop length attacks; motivates token- or KV-based admission.

column2: Denial-of-Service Poisoning Attacks against Large Language Models
column8: injecting a single poisoned sample designed for DoS purposes can break the output length limit
column9: Fine-tuning-time poisoning (P-DoS) makes models emit repeated output up to max inference length, including via a commercial fine-tuning API.
column10: Output length only, via training-data poisoning; no KV cache, prefix cache, eviction, or compression; no multi-tenant measurement.
column11: Background for length-inflation class; not a serving-system attack.

column2: ReasoningBomb: A Stealthy Denial-of-Service Attack by Inducing Pathologically Long Reasoning in Large Reasoning Models
column8: ReasoningBomb induces 18,759 completion tokens on average and 19,263 reasoning tokens on average across reasoning models.
column9: Short prompts induce very long reasoning with large input-to-output amplification, beating prior baselines.
column10: Token/compute inflation only; no KV cache, prefix, eviction, or compression targeting; abstract reports no effect on other users or throughput.
column11: Crowded area: reasoning-length DoS has several 2025-2026 papers (OverThink, ThinkTrap, ReasoningBomb).

column2: The Multi-Tenant LLM Problem: Noisy Neighbors, Isolation, and Fairness at Scale
column8: One tenant's expensive session evicts another tenant's KV cache, forcing recomputation.
column9: Practitioner acknowledgement that cross-tenant KV eviction raises victim TTFT; argues for token-based rate limiting.
column10: Opinion piece with no measurement of cross-tenant eviction harm; benign noisy neighbor, not adversarial; no compression.
column11: Evidence the problem is felt in practice but unmeasured; supports a measurement contribution.

column2: CVE-2026-10813: LMCache 16-bit Multimodal Hash Collision Vulnerability
column8: A flaw has been identified in LMCache versions up to 0.4.6.
column9: LMCache KV handler uses a weak 16-bit hash (hex_hash_to_int16) that allows cache poisoning of KV data in the offload tier.
column10: Integrity (collision/poisoning) of the LMCache tier, not exhaustion or eviction; local, high complexity; no other-tenant availability measurement; aggregator page, NVD not opened.
column11: Only offload-tier security item found; offload-tier availability (thrashing CPU/disk tiers) appears unstudied.

column2: Locality-aware Fair Scheduling in LLM Serving
column8: fail to take prefix locality into consideration
column9: DLPM/D2LPM scheduling keeps prefix locality while giving a fairness guarantee; up to 2.87x throughput over VTC.
column10: Benign fairness vs locality tradeoff; no adversarial tenant gaming locality or polluting the prefix cache; fairness is over service, not cache occupancy.
column11: Open question: can an adversary exploit locality-aware schedulers (prefix matching priority) to gain share or evict others.

column2: vLLM through 0.29.0 Resource Exhaustion via Ownerless Mooncake Transfer Placeholders (CVE-2026-94625)
column8: causing valid requests to be delayed by up to 480 seconds
column9: Disaggregated prefill/decode KV transfer path in vLLM has a remotely triggerable resource leak that delays other users' valid requests while health checks pass.
column10: Implementation bug in KV transfer bookkeeping (Mooncake), not KV cache occupancy, prefix cache, eviction, or compression policy; does affect other users.
column11: Shows KV transfer/offload layers are a live 2026 DoS surface in vLLM; disclosure precedent.

column2: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
column8: this memory can be significantly wasted by fragmentation and redundant duplication
column9: Defines paged KV memory, sharing, and preemption (swap/recompute) mechanisms that later DoS attacks exploit.
column10: Not a security paper; no adversary, no tenant isolation.
column11: System background for preemption and block-level sharing.

column2: Optimization and Tuning (vLLM v0.19.0 docs, Preemption section)
column8: In such cases, vLLM can preempt requests to free up KV cache space for other requests.
column9: vLLM V1 preempts with RECOMPUTE by default when KV space is insufficient; operator levers are global (gpu_memory_utilization, max_num_seqs, TP).
column10: Docs only; section mentions no per-tenant KV quota, isolation, or fairness; no adversary.
column11: Confirms stock vLLM has no per-tenant KV quota, the condition F&S exploits.

column2: KVCache Cache in the Wild: Characterizing and Optimizing KVCache Cache at a Large Cloud Provider
column8: KV$ reuses are skewed across requests
column9: Production trace characterization of KV-cache reuse and a workload-aware eviction policy; cited by PrefixShield as source of one-touch pollution pattern.
column10: Benign workloads only; no tenants, interference, or adversarial pollution per the abstract page.
column11: Provides realistic traces/baselines for a pollution study; eviction policy itself could be attacked.

column2: Rerouting LLM Routers
column8: query-independent token sequences we call ``confounder gadgets''
column9: Gadget strings force model-selection routers to send queries to the expensive model, white-box and black-box.
column10: Model-selection (cost) routers, not prefix-aware or KV-cache-aware load balancers; no KV, eviction, or compression; no other-tenant load measurement.
column11: Attacks on prefix-aware/cache-affinity request routers (vLLM production-stack, llm-d) appear unstudied in this search.

column2: Cache Me, Catch You: Cache Related Security Threats in LLM Serving Frameworks
column8: manipulate cache entries to deliver malicious content to users via prefix cache collisions
column9: Prefix-cache collision and poisoning vectors exist in vLLM, SGLang, and other frameworks; disclosed and partly fixed.
column10: Integrity attacks on prefix cache; page excerpt mentions no availability, DoS, or eviction.
column11: Neighbor class (integrity); combine with pollution for availability is unclaimed.

column2: Equinox: Holistic Fair Scheduling in Serving Large Language Models
column8: We address the limitations of current LLM serving with a dual-counter framework separating user and operator perspectives.
column9: Fair scheduling with user and operator counters using predicted tokens and latency.
column10: No adversarial users mentioned; fairness of service, not KV memory or prefix cache.
column11: Fairness line keeps growing without an adversarial KV-occupancy model.

column2: Ensuring Fair LLM Serving Amid Diverse Applications
column8: some users may submit an excessive number of requests
column9: FairServe uses application-aware throttling and weighted service counters to curb abusive usage on a production multi-tenant platform (MS CoPilot traces).
column10: Abuse modeled as request volume/tokens, not KV occupancy, prefix eviction, or compression manipulation.
column11: Closest fairness work that names abusive users; still not memory-aware.

column2: LoopLLM: Transferable Energy-Latency Attacks in LLMs via Repetitive Generation
column8: achieving over 90% of the maximum output length, compared to 20% for baselines
column9: Repetition-inducing prompts reach near max output length and transfer to commercial models.
column10: Output length only; no KV cache, prefix, eviction, or compression; no multi-tenant measurement (F&S uses it as a baseline and finds small TTFT impact).
column11: Model-level length attacks are mature.

column2: CVE-2026-94624: vLLM P2P KV Offloading DoS Vulnerability
column8: The resulting uncaught ZMQError crashes EngineCore and halts all inference on the affected instance.
column9: vLLM P2P KV offloading path through 0.29.0 can be crashed remotely via crafted kv_transfer_params, halting all tenants on the instance.
column10: Input-validation bug in the offload connector, not a cache-policy or eviction attack; no compression; aggregator page, NVD not opened.
column11: KV offload/transfer connectors are a fresh bug surface; fuzzing them is engineering, not research novelty.

column2: CVE-2026-94627: vLLM Mooncake Connector DOS Vulnerability
column8: Blocks belonging to sibling requests become orphaned and remain resident in GPU memory.
column9: KV block ownership bug in disaggregated serving leaks GPU KV blocks until restart, eventually blocking legitimate requests.
column10: Leak bug in KV bookkeeping, not policy-level eviction or compression; aggregator page.
column11: Another KV-memory availability bug; shows KV accounting correctness under adversarial request shapes is weak.
